questions.subject: MATH
questions.learningObjective: Solve problems involving set operations and identities.
questions.stem: A set A has 7 elements, a set B has 10 elements, and their intersection has 1 elements. How many elements are in A union B?

options.misconception: Wrong belief "adds the sizes without removing the overlap" gives 17, not 16.
Wrong belief "subtracts the intersection twice" gives 15, not 16.
Wrong belief "subtracts the smaller set entirely" gives 3, not 16.

questions.explanation: By inclusion-exclusion, the size of the union is the size of A plus the size of B minus the size of their intersection, namely 7 + 10 - 1 which equals 16.
questions.hint: Add the two sizes, then subtract the shared elements once.

questions.stem: A set A has 5 elements, a set B has 4 elements, and their intersection has 1 elements. How many elements are in A union B?

questions.hint: Add the two sizes, then subtract the shared elements once.
